references.text: The children of Israel ate manna for forty years until they came to inhabited land—a parallel to the forty years in the wilderness mentioned in Deuteronomy.
Describes the forty years Israel wandered in the wilderness as a consequence of their disobedience, where each year represented a day the spies explored the land.
Mentions that Aaron died in the fortieth year after the Israelites left Egypt, confirming the forty years in the wilderness.
Continues the theme of God testing and humbling Israel in the wilderness, where He gave them manna to test them.
Concerns keeping the Lord's commands and the testing of the heart, which is central in Deuteronomy 8:2.
The Lord tested Israel at Marah, which is an example of the trials mentioned in Deuteronomy 8:2.
Moses explains that God came to test the people so that the fear of Him would be upon them and they would not sin.
Refers to the forty years God was angry with the wilderness generation because they did not know His ways.
Quotes Psalm 95 about the forty years in the wilderness where God was tested by the fathers, and they saw His works.
Stephen mentions that Moses led the people out and performed wonders for forty years in the wilderness.
Paul notes that God bore with them in the wilderness for about forty years.
Jesus is led into the wilderness to be tempted and quotes from Deuteronomy 8 when He answers Satan.
